intel.t: Main message: working class populism from a former labor leader who will not caucus with either party, asking voters to take off the red and blue jerseys.

Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it: Republicans call him Democrat Dan, a secret Democrat funded by coastal donors, and point to FEC complaints over payments to family. He denies being a Democrat and calls the complaints baseless.
Strongest coalition: cross party working class voters and farm groups, including the Nebraska Farmers Union endorsement, with about 71,000 donors.
Polls: YouGov had him up 48 to 47 from September 24 to October 3, SurveyUSA up 46 to 42, and co/efficient had Ricketts up 48 to 43.
Notable recent event: Trump rallied for Ricketts in Grand Island on October 5, and the Senate Leadership Fund is adding $8M through Election Day.
Outside air cover: $12.8M from six groups through October 13.
Main message: Osborn is a secret Democrat, Democrat Dan, backed by coastal liberal donors, while Ricketts says he cannot be bought and touts the 2025 tax law and tariffs for agriculture.
Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it: a billionaire family incumbent who funds himself and dark money, in Osborn's telling; Ricketts put $5.2M of his own money in during one quarter.
Strongest coalition: rural and agricultural Nebraska, with a Farm Bureau endorsement and most large gifts from Nebraskans.
Polls: within 5 points either way in three late September and early October surveys, the best for him co/efficient at 48 to 43.
Notable recent event: Trump campaigned for him in Grand Island on October 5, and Senate Republicans are adding $8M through Election Day.
Air war: $7.9M for him or against Osborn through October 1 against $7.3M the other way.

Interviewed Dan Osborn on What Next about why he is running as an independent.

Hosted a live Prof G conversation with independent Dan Osborn about his race against Pete Ricketts.
Predicted Pete Ricketts will win and called Dan Osborn a phony.

research.summary: Independent Dan Osborn, a former Kellogg's mechanic and union leader, is in what IVN calls a toss up with Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts, with recent polls ranging from a one point Osborn edge to a four point Ricketts lead. Ricketts and national Republicans brand him Democrat Dan and press his leaked Red Cloud remarks, while Osborn hits the Iran war, costs and money in politics and says he will caucus with neither party.

issues.why: Ricketts touts the tax law's cuts and a housing bill, while Osborn says the law favors the wealthy and the Iran war is raising gas, diesel and grocery prices.
Both oppose Trump's plan to let in foreign beef without high tariffs, but Ricketts backs tariffs broadly while Osborn wants targeted ones and congressional control.
Ricketts defends new Medicaid rules while Osborn cites a dialysis closure in Chadron as proof the changes hurt rural Nebraska.
Ricketts says Osborn is a Democrat in disguise, and Osborn pledges not to caucus with either party.
Fertilizer prices spiked with the Iran war, and Vance announced a federal ammonia plant investment in Nebraska while campaigning for Ricketts.

storylines.title: Fresh money and polls show a toss up
storylines.what: Osborn has raised 9.8 million dollars and Ricketts 14.5 million, with Ricketts holding less cash on hand, and recent polls split narrowly.

storylines.title: Vance campaigns in North Platte
storylines.what: Vance called Osborn a far left partisan Democrat and announced a fertilizer plant investment, and Osborn's campaign said Ricketts needs Trump, Vance and Thune to save him.

storylines.title: Osborn ad hits Trump beef import plan
storylines.what: Osborn aired an ad attacking Trump's plan to bring in foreign beef, a plan Ricketts also opposes.

storylines.title: Trump rallies in Grand Island
storylines.what: Trump held a rally for Ricketts in Grand Island, an unusual move for a Republican incumbent in Nebraska.

storylines.title: Osborn apologizes in Red Cloud
storylines.what: After leaked audio of Osborn mocking a hypothetical Red Cloud Trump voter became a Ricketts ad, Osborn returned to apologize and residents gave mixed reactions.

storylines.title: Only debate at the State Fair
storylines.what: Ricketts repeatedly called Osborn Democrat Dan and defended tariffs and Medicaid changes, while Osborn hit grocery costs, super PACs and rural health cuts.

events.title: The Red Cloud tape
events.prompt: Leaked audio of the independent mocking a hypothetical small town Trump voter is now in an attack ad. How does the campaign handle it?

opts.label: Dismiss as distraction
opts.say: Say the tape was taken out of context and turn to the incumbent's family money.

opts.label: Go back and apologize
opts.say: Return to the town, apologize face to face and take questions on property taxes and veterans.

opts.label: Run it statewide
opts.say: Air the audio everywhere as proof the opponent looks down on rural Nebraska.

events.title: Democrat Dan label
events.prompt: The Republican says the independent is a Democrat in disguise, citing ActBlue fundraising and the state party's backing. How does the campaign define itself?

opts.label: Embrace the coalition
opts.say: Welcome Democratic support and argue a broad anti establishment coalition is needed to win.

opts.label: Caucus with nobody
opts.say: Pledge to answer to neither party and work with a bloc of independents.

opts.label: Tie him to Schumer
opts.say: Argue a vote for the independent is a vote for a Democratic Senate majority.

events.title: Beef imports and tariffs
events.prompt: The president plans to let in foreign beef with lower tariffs, angering cattle ranchers. What is the trade stance?

opts.label: Congress takes tariffs back
opts.say: Call the beef plan a colossal mistake and say Congress should control tariff power.

opts.label: Oppose beef plan only
opts.say: Back tariffs generally but push a herd rebuilding plan and oppose the beef waiver.

opts.label: Stand with the president
opts.say: Defend the president's trade agenda as fair to farmers in the long run.

events.title: Rural clinic closures
events.prompt: A dialysis center closed in Chadron as Medicaid rules change. What is the health care position?

opts.label: Reverse the cuts
opts.say: Say the Medicaid changes are closing rural care and must be undone.

opts.label: Rural care fund
opts.say: Keep the reforms but push dedicated funding for rural hospitals and clinics.

opts.label: Defend reforms
opts.say: Argue the changes protect Medicaid for people who are truly eligible.

ads.theme: Uses leaked audio of Osborn mocking a Red Cloud Trump voter to argue he looks down on rural Nebraska.
Attacks Trump's plan to import foreign beef as bad for Nebraska ranchers.

regions.name: Omaha metro
regions.note: The largest vote center, with Democratic leaning Omaha and Republican suburbs that Osborn needs to win big.

regions.name: Lincoln
regions.note: The capital and university town leans Democratic, with Republican rural neighbors.

regions.name: Northeast Nebraska
regions.note: Manufacturing and meatpacking towns where Osborn's union message is tested.

regions.name: Central and Tri Cities
regions.note: Republican farm and ranch country including Grand Island, Kearney, North Platte and Red Cloud.

regions.name: Panhandle and Sandhills
regions.note: The most Republican part of the state, where rural health access and cattle prices dominate.
